sections.h2: What the Register of Deeds does for a seller
sections.html:
This is the office that records the deed passing title to your buyer. It also holds the lasting county-wide index of deeds, deeds of trust, plats and easements. Staff do recording only. They may not practice law under state law, which rules out legal forms and explanations of what a document does. Your closing attorney handles that.

Graham is the seat and Burlington the largest community. Properties in Burlington, Mebane, Elon, Haw River and the rest of the county's thirteen townships all go through this one office. The county has 83,187 housing units (July 2025), and with 186,177 residents the office stays busy with conveyances.

The front counter is open from 8:00 to 5:00 on weekdays, but the last submission for recording is 4:30. That cutoff dates from August 2013, when the county adopted G.S. 153A-94(b). The phone menu has separate options for recording help, for earlier recorded documents, and for vital records.

Recording a deed runs $26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for each page beyond. A deed of trust starts from a longer base, and its figure was reset effective October 1, 2016.

Recording and copy fees at the Alamance County Register of Deeds

Vital records such as marriage licenses and certified birth, death and marriage certificates are paid in cash or by money order only. Before you go, ask which payment types the office accepts for recording.

sections.h2: North Carolina excise tax on a deed
sections.html:
Each conveyance is taxed by the state at $1.00 per $500 of value, with a fraction of $500 counted whole. Under G.S. 105-228.30, the transferor pays the register of deeds before recording. For a parcel in more than one county, payment goes where most of the value lies.

Proceeds go from the register to the county finance officer. The county general fund keeps half, and the rest goes to the state once refunds and the county's collection allowance are taken out. The same statute covers timber deeds.

You will not see this tax on the county fee schedule, because it is a state levy separate from the recording charge. Your settlement attorney reads the consideration off the deed and collects the tax with the fee. Ask to see the figure on your settlement statement before closing day.

Paper deeds must satisfy G.S. 161-14(b), and the office repeats the rules on its recording page. A deed that falls short still gets recorded, for an extra $25.

  • Sheets of 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Three blank inches above the first page text, with half an inch minimum elsewhere on page one and on all edges of later pages.
  • Black print on white paper, with nine point as the smallest legible font. Pen is allowed for blanks and corrections.
  • Printing on one side only.
  • The instrument's title at the top of page one, under the margin.

Plats follow a separate rule: mylar only, cut to 18 by 24 inches. Enclose a stamped self-addressed envelope sized for the recorded document.

Staff stamp each instrument with the day and hour it arrived and record in arrival order. The statute allows up to 30 days to finish indexing. Keep the book and page number the county assigns, since that is how you will refer to the document later.

One step surprises some sellers because it comes first. Deeds recorded since May 2, 2011 (timber deeds and releases excepted) pass through the county Tax Department for a delinquent tax certification. Overdue county tax stalls recording until it is paid, so ask for a payoff early.

Electronic recording has been available since November 2015 for everything but plats, so your attorney can submit through a vendor. After recording, Land Records at the Tax Department revises the owner name and mailing address. Straight sales move quicker than splits. Call with your book and page number if nothing changes after several weeks.

sections.h2: Other county offices in a house sale
sections.html:
Three other offices usually touch a sale, and each keeps a different slice of the record.

  • Tax Department, Land Records: at 124 W. Elm St. in Graham, phone (336) 228-1312. It owns the parcel's owner name, mailing address and tax map, and staff want the book and page number of any recorded deed when you call about a change.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: holds estate filings and court orders, which establish who owns a house after a death or a court proceeding. When title runs through an estate, the clerk files the estate papers and this office records the deeds the heirs or the court sign.
  • North Carolina Secretary of State: holds business filings. A merger, name change or dissolution alters how a company-owned parcel is listed.

Names on the county record follow the recorded deed letter for letter. A misspelling on the deed itself needs a corrected document recorded here, and a lawyer can prepare it. A marriage or court-ordered name change does not alter the owner name unless a new document is recorded.

Tax bills are mailed in July and due September 1, so changing a mailing address before July keeps the bill from going astray after you sell.

sections.h2: How to search or copy land records
sections.html:
Search recorded deeds by name through the office's online search, and go to the office itself for certified copies. Online records are unofficial, and the paper records in the office are the official ones.

  • Certified copies: $5 for page one, $2 for each page after it.
  • Plain copies: $0.25 a page.
  • Owner, mailing address and legal description: the Tax Department's property record search.
  • Tax maps are drawn for assessment and are not surveys. Hire a surveyor and use the recorded plat for any boundary question.

Paying off a mortgage? Have the lender record the release, since cancellation of a deed of trust is itself a recorded instrument.

sections.h2: Getting ready to record your sale
sections.html: Work backward from the 4:30 cutoff. Ask your closing attorney whether the deed will go by electronic recording or on paper. If it is paper, check the margins, font size and one-sided printing against the formatting list above. Confirm that the tax certification has cleared, and that the excise tax and recording fee are collected at closing. Afterward, keep the book and page number, and update your mailing address with Land Records so a bill does not go to the wrong place.

faqs.q: What is the last time of day to record a deed in Alamance County?
faqs.a: Documents must come in by 4:30 p.m. The doors stay open until 5:00, yet the recording cutoff comes half an hour earlier under G.S. 153A-94(b).

faqs.q: Who pays North Carolina's deed excise tax?
faqs.a: The transferor pays it before recording. G.S. 105-228.30 sets $1.00 per $500 of value, rounding any part of $500 up.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed here?
faqs.a: A deed costs $26 through page 15, then $4 per added page. Documents that miss the formatting rules carry a $25 surcharge.

faqs.q: Is electronic recording offered in Alamance County?
faqs.a: Yes, for every document except plats, since November 2015. Closing attorneys normally submit through a recording vendor.

faqs.q: Why did my deed have to go to the Tax Department first?
faqs.a: Deeds recorded after May 2, 2011, other than timber deeds and releases, need delinquent tax certification from the county Tax Department before recording. Unpaid county tax must be cleared first.
